---

## 3. `ExpectedName`: an optional field guarding a documented no-prompt install path

**The special case.** `plugin_install_remote.go:42-47`. Empty string means "no expectation"; three production callers set it (`plugin_group.go:221`, `plugin_deps.go:244`, `plugin_install_remote.go:245`), and one of those sets it to `""` on the URL branch.

**Why the mechanism is wrong-level.** The comment at `plugin_install_remote.go:113-128` documents three concrete failures a forgotten field reopens — including "the index entry says `safe`, the repo declares `hijack`, and the user gets `entire-hijack` on PATH with no prompt", because index installs never prompt (`plugin_group.go:186`). A guard that severe should not be defeatable by omission in a struct literal.

**The deeper fix.** Split the API to match a distinction that is already real in the domain — index/dependency/upgrade installs are "install plugin *X*, whose repo I looked up"; URL installs are "install whatever is at this URL", and they differ in trust handling too:

```
InstallKnownPlugin(ctx, name string, opts)   // name required, validated non-empty
InstallPluginFromURL(ctx, url string, opts)  // no expectation, remote names itself
```

Both delegate to an unexported `installFromRepo(ctx, repoURL, expectedName string, opts)`. Purely a signature change; no behavior moves. The compiler then forces every caller to pick a side, and `""` is not expressible on the path where it matters. A plain required parameter is the cheaper half-measure — better than today, but `""` stays typeable.

**Cost of leaving it:** one forgotten field in one future call site silently reopens a no-prompt name-substitution hole. There is no test that can catch the *absence* of a field in a caller that doesn't exist yet.

---

## 4. `plugin doctor` vs `entire doctor`: separate command is correct; two shared-level gaps

I checked for an extension point. **There is none** — `entire doctor`'s checks are hardcoded calls in `runSessionsFix` (`doctor.go:95`, `:106`, `:109`, `:113`). So "register with the existing mechanism" isn't available; the only options are a separate command or another hardcoded call.

**Separate command is the right call, for reasons that hold up:**
- **Scope mismatch.** `entire doctor` is repo-scoped and hard-fails outside a repo (`doctor.go:127` `openRepository`, `doctor.go:359` same, `doctor.go:468` `paths.WorktreeRoot`). Plugin health is per-user/per-machine (managed dir under `XDG_DATA_HOME`/`LOCALAPPDATA`). Folding it in would make plugin health uncheckable outside a git repo — where a plugin problem is just as likely.
- **Exit-code contract mismatch.** `plugin doctor` returns non-zero on any issue (`plugin_group.go:681`). `entire doctor` is warn-only/interactive-fix and returns 0 for advisory findings. Merging would either make plugin warnings fail `entire doctor` or silently downgrade `plugin doctor`'s script-usable exit code.

**Two additive gaps at the existing altitude, no new abstraction needed:**

- `entire doctor`'s enumerated check list (`doctor.go:33-49`) never mentions plugin health, and neither does `doctor.go` anywhere (verified: zero occurrences of "plugin" in `doctor.go`, `doctor_bundle.go`, `doctor_logs.go`). A warn-only `checkPluginHealth(cmd)` next to `checkCodexHookTrust`/`checkClaudeCodeHookDrift` would fit exactly — those are already warn-only, non-fatal, and return silently when not applicable (`doctor.go:468-474`). Or at minimum a one-line pointer.
- `doctor bundle` collects no plugin state at all (`doctor_bundle.go:104-133`: logs, `.entire/settings*.json`, git status/log/remote, refs, version). A support bundle from a user with a broken plugin install contains nothing about it. `ListPluginManifests()` rendered through one `addStringToZip` call matches the existing `entireRefsReport`/`versionInfoString` precedent, and `redactBundleEntry` (`doctor_bundle.go:280`) already scrubs contents on the way in.

---

## 5. `validatePluginRepoURL`: right altitude. Leave it.

I traced every git invocation that receives a URL:

| Site | Validated |
|---|---|
| `plugin_gitremote.go:146` `ls-remote --tags --refs -- <url>` | `:141` |
| `plugin_gitremote.go:219/223/228` `clone ... -- <url> <tmp>` | `:204` |
| `plugin_index.go:223` `clone --depth 1 --quiet -- <url> <dir>` | `:169` |
| `plugin_gitremote.go:234` `-C <tmp> show` | no URL |
| `plugin_index.go:242/245` `-C <dir> fetch origin HEAD` / `reset --hard` | no URL (uses `origin`) |

**There is no present hole.** And the design is the textbook one: validate at *data ingress* (`loadPluginIndexFromDir:295`, which drops bad catalog entries rather than failing the whole catalog — a behavior a sink check structurally cannot provide) *and* at the sink. The three sink calls are the belt to the ingress braces, and each produces a differently-scoped message (`SyncPluginIndex:170` prefixes `"plugin index URL:"`).

Moving it into `runGitQuiet` is feasible — all three URL-bearing sites use the `--` convention, so "validate the first positional after a bare `--`" would work in ~6 lines — but it buys only protection for a *future* call site, at the cost of flattening those distinct messages. This is one of the places where N explicit call sites genuinely beats hidden magic: it's a security check, and the explicitness is doing work. If you want the backstop anyway, add it *in addition* rather than removing the current three.

---

## 6. `requireSecureAssetURL`: right altitude, and a transport-level move would be a net regression

`pluginHTTPClient` is package-private and touched by exactly two functions — `httpGetSmall:378` and `fetchAndVerify:422` — plus its own `CheckRedirect:100`. The check is called at all three (`:371`, `:415`, `:100`). That is a complete funnel, not a leaky one.

A `http.RoundTripper` would be more future-proof (a hypothetical third `Do` site couldn't forget), but it makes the outcome *worse* in a way the current design gets right: a `RoundTrip` error is wrapped by the client into `*url.Error`, and `net/http/client.go:629`'s `stripPassword` only removes the password — the token-as-username form survives. Today the check runs pre-flight, so the carefully-worded message at `plugin_fetch.go:64` (which explains *why* plaintext defeats checksum verification) is what the user sees, with the URL already through `redactURL`. Keep it.

The one hardening worth noting is a non-change: the invariant is "nothing calls `pluginHTTPClient.Do` except these two functions", and package-privacy already enforces it as well as anything short of a linter.

---

## 7. `pluginBinaryName` / `windowsExeExt`: correctly generalized

I traced construct / match / parse for round-trip consistency:

- **Construct:** `pluginBinaryName` (`plugin_manifest.go:38`) → `entire-<name>` + `.exe` on Windows. Used at `plugin_install_remote.go:152` and `plugin_deps.go:383`.
- **Match:** `matchesPluginBinary` (`plugin_fetch.go:487`) → exact, or `+.exe` case-insensitively on Windows.
- **Parse:** `bareNameFromBinaryName` (`plugin_store.go:536`, **pre-existing**) → strips `.exe/.bat/.cmd/.com` via `external.StripExeExt`.

Construct→parse round-trips on Windows (`entire-foo.exe` → `foo`), and `plugin_install_remote.go:177` feeds the constructed `pkgBin` straight into the pre-existing `InstallPluginFromPath`, so the wider extension set that `plugin_store.go` handles for *user-supplied* binaries doesn't need duplicating for *CLI-written* ones. The construction side legitimately only ever needs `.exe`, and `external` exposes no construction helper to reuse.

The remaining platform branches are each localized with a documented rationale and are not scattered: `plugin_fetch.go:158`/`:172` (darwin asset-name aliases, with the `darwin_all` bug write-up), `plugin_install_remote.go:269` (Windows rename-aside), `plugin_deps.go:414` (darwin quarantine).

Two low-priority locality nits: `windowsExeExt` is defined in `plugin_manifest.go:33` but used mostly from `plugin_fetch.go`; and `darwinGOOS` was added to `explain.go:55` beside the pre-existing `windowsGOOS`, which is an odd home for shared platform constants. The branch propagated a pre-existing misplacement rather than creating one, and staying consistent with `windowsGOOS` was the better of the two available choices. Also minor: `matchesPluginBinary` is case-*sensitive* on the no-extension branch and case-*insensitive* on the `.exe` branch, so on Windows `ENTIRE-FOO.EXE` matches but `ENTIRE-FOO` doesn't.

content.text:
Cleanup applied and pushed as `abf3a923f`. `mise run test:ci` green, lint 0 issues.

## Fixed

Two of these were **regressions, not tidiness** — both in code I wrote yesterday:

- **Redaction was leaking query strings.** My local `redactURL` stripped userinfo but kept the query. Release hosts redirect asset downloads to signed CDN URLs, so `?token=` / `X-Amz-Signature=` would have reached error messages — and my "credentials never leak" test passed anyway because it only tested userinfo. Now delegates to `gitremote.RedactURL`, the repo-wide helper that already strips both. **Five call sites had also been missed**, including both of `validatePluginRepoURL`'s own rejection messages, which echo the URL being rejected.
- **`runGitQuiet` clobbered `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`.** Setting it unconditionally discarded a user's own ssh invocation and `core.sshCommand` — the exact problem `checkpoint/remote/git.go` exists to solve, documented there as issue #1523. Now supplied only when unset.

The rest were genuine cleanups: `dependencySatisfied` returns the manifest it loaded (three reads per requirement → one, two duplicated blocks gone); `downloadPluginAsset` resolves the URL prefix once instead of re-parsing per candidate and carrying an error return through three call sites; `--index` collapsed from five registrations to one helper; the duplicated index sync hoisted out of both branches; and the integration fixture's stale `requires[].repo_url` now points at an unreachable host so it proves the ignore path instead of implying the field still works.

## Skipped, with reasons

**Behavior risk:** carrying the resolved tag from `planDeps` into the install (would suppress the tag-fallback walk for pushed-but-unpublished releases — the biggest efficiency win at ~1.5–3s per dependency, but not a cleanup); `HEAD`-probing before download (needs a 405 fallback); parallelizing `upgrade --all` (adds an errgroup to a rare command).

**Outside the diff:** promoting `silencePluginCancel` to `errors.go` and collapsing the three other copies; adding a redaction pass at `main.go`'s print boundary — this one is the strongest remaining idea, because `%w`-wrapped `url.Error` leaks the full credentialed URL no matter how disciplined the call sites are, and one line there would cover every site including future ones. I did fix the comment that cited `activity_cmd.go` as precedent; that file contains no such pattern.

**Wants your call:** splitting `InstallPluginFromRepo` into `InstallKnownPlugin` / `InstallPluginFromURL` so `ExpectedName` can't be forgotten. Sound argument — an optional field guards a no-prompt install path — but it's a public API shape change I'd rather Thomas weighed in on.

**Largest remaining item:** ~215 lines of test-helper duplication. Two near-identical release servers, four repo-fixture builders, two tar.gz writers, and a 4-line preamble repeated eight times. It needs helpers moved into `testutil` to cross the unit/integration package boundary — worth doing, but it's a test-only refactor bigger than the production cleanup was.

One thing the reuse angle surfaced that's worth knowing regardless: the repo has **six** copies of "add a `v`, then `semver.Compare`" and **five** copies of "extract stderr from `exec.ExitError`". My `canonicalSemver` and `stderrSuffix` are just the newest of each. Consolidating those is a repo-wide cleanup, not this branch's job.

You're right to push — I was wrong about most of it. All seven test files are **new in this PR** (`A` status), and `testutil` is untouched by the branch:

```
A  cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/plugin_remote_install_test.go
A  cmd/entire/cli/plugin_deps_test.go
A  cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch_test.go
A  cmd/entire/cli/plugin_gitremote_test.go
A  cmd/entire/cli/plugin_index_test.go
A  cmd/entire/cli/plugin_install_remote_test.go
A  cmd/entire/cli/plugin_manifest_test.go
```

So the duplication is entirely self-inflicted by this branch, not shared with pre-existing tests. My "reaches outside the diff" justification was wrong for the bulk of it.

**What's actually in scope.** Six of the seven files are `package cli`, so they can be deduped among themselves touching nothing pre-existing — roughly 140–150 of the ~215 lines:

- `updateRepoMetadata` (15 lines of hand-rolled `git add` + `git -c user.name=… commit`) when the *same file* already does that correctly in 5 lines with `testutil.WriteFile`/`GitAdd`/`GitCommit`
- the `srv` + `defer Close` + `meta` + `repoURL` preamble repeated 8× (~32 lines), with the `download_url` format string written 10 times
- ~6 of the 13 ad-hoc `httptest` servers in `plugin_fetch_test.go`, two of which are byte-identical pairs
- `withPluginDir` + `withIsolatedPath` always paired, 20 times
- `t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", t.TempDir())` 8 times
- direct `os.WriteFile`/`os.MkdirAll` where pre-existing `testutil.WriteFile` already creates parents

That last group is *using* pre-existing helpers more, not changing them — which is the opposite of reaching outside the diff.

**What genuinely does reach outside** is only the unit↔integration sharing, ~65–75 lines: `pluginReleaseServer` vs `startReleaseServer` (18 lines byte-identical), `newTaggedPluginRepo` vs `newPluginRepo`, the two `newIndexRepo`s with the same name and different signatures, and `makeTarGz` vs `makeScriptTarGz`. Unexported `_test.go` helpers can't cross packages, so those need a home in `testutil` — a shared package many other suites depend on.

There's also one real correctness angle hiding in here, which is why I'd not leave it all: the three `git tag` shell-outs and the bare-repo init set no `cmd.Env`, so they inherit the developer's global git config. A developer with `tag.gpgSign=true` would see those tests fail locally. The pre-existing `testutil.CreateBranch` and `GitReset` handle this by passing `GitIsolatedEnv()` per command — the new helpers just didn't follow the pattern.

My suggestion: do the in-package portion now, since it's squarely the changed code, and add the `GitIsolatedEnv()` to the tag/bare-init shell-outs while I'm there. Leave the cross-package `testutil` consolidation as a separate call — it's a shared-package change that's worth doing only if that release-server logic drifts again, and it'd be cleaner as its own commit.

Want me to do the in-package half?

So I did the third.

## What changed

`RemoteInstallOptions` carried `RepoURL` and `ExpectedName` as fields. Neither is an option — one is the target, the other is a security decision. Both are now required arguments:

```go
InstallPluginFromRepo(ctx, repoURL, expectedName string, opts RemoteInstallOptions)
```

The struct is down to the three genuine options: `Pin`, `Force`, `AllowUnverified`.

The point isn't cosmetic. `ExpectedName` as a field could be silently omitted, and omitting it reopens the hole it exists to close — an index entry named `safe` installing `entire-hijack`, or `--force` on plugin A replacing an unrelated installed B. And no test can catch a field missing from a caller that doesn't exist yet. As an argument, `""` is still expressible but it's a visible choice rather than an omission.

## Where I didn't follow the reviewer

The altitude agent wanted two functions — `InstallKnownPlugin` and `InstallPluginFromURL` — so the compiler forces the choice. I didn't, and the reason is specific: two of three callers always know the name, but `runRemoteInstall` legitimately handles both cases. Splitting would move the `""` into a branch there rather than eliminate it, so you'd get the same residual expressiveness for twice the exported surface. I noted that trade in the commit so the next reader doesn't re-derive it.

The `main.go` print-boundary redaction is still the strongest idea from the whole `/simplify` pass, and worth flagging to Thomas for a follow-up: `%w`-wrapped `url.Error` prints the full credentialed URL regardless of how disciplined the call sites are, because `net/url.Error.Error()` does no redaction. One line at `main.go`'s error print would cover every current site, the five I'd missed, and every future one. It's a global change to error output, so it wants its own PR and its own thought about what else it might scrub.

The `silencePluginCancel` promotion is lower value — four copies of a 3-line convention, where the newest (mine) is the best of them because of the `ctx.Err()` check the other three lack. Also a follow-up on pre-existing files.

input.content:
## Summary

Expands the kubectl-style external-command layer so users can discover and install plugins without cloning anything, from any git host. 18 files, ~5,540 insertions.

- **Remote install** — `entire plugin install <name|url|path>`. Newest **stable** semver tag via `git ls-remote` (forge-agnostic, inherits git auth and proxies; no forge REST client anywhere). Optional `entire-plugin.yml` metadata read via blobless shallow clone. Release assets download over HTTPS through a small per-host URL convention table (GitHub/Gitea-style, GitLab-style, `download_url` template escape hatch), selected and verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. Binaries land in `pkg/<name>/` with a provenance `manifest.yml`; `bin/` stays the only dispatch surface and the resolver in `plugin.go` is untouched.
- **Upgrade** — `entire plugin upgrade [name|--all]`, `--pin` to hold a tag, next-highest-tag fallback for pushed-but-unpublished releases, Windows locked-binary rename-aside.
- **Discovery** — krew-style git-synced index ([entireio/plugin-index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index)): shallow-cloned into the user cache keyed by URL hash, flock-guarded, 24h TTL, stale-copy-on-offline. New `search`/`info`/`browse`/`index update` subcommands; bare-name installs resolve through the index. Index URL: `--index` > `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` > built-in default.
- **Dependencies** — `entire-plugin.yml` `requires` (`name` + optional `min_version`, no ranges), resolved by name through the index. Install-time transitive planning, apt-style single confirmation, remove guard for depended-on plugins, and `entire plugin doctor`. Dispatch stays zero-cost — no runtime dependency checks.

## Security model

This code ends in downloading a binary and making it executable, so the trust boundaries are the design:

- **Transport.** HTTPS required for anything off-machine, re-validated on every redirect hop (Go follows redirects across schemes; validating only the entry point is bypassable). Loopback exempt so `httptest` fixtures work.
- **Authentication.** A release that publishes no `checksums.txt` for the platform is **refused by default**; `--allow-unverified` opts in, is recorded in the manifest, reported by `doctor`, and inherited by `upgrade`.
- **Integrity.** The installed binary's digest is recorded as `binary_sha256` and re-checked by `doctor`. (`sha256` covers the downloaded *asset*, which is discarded with the staging dir — provenance only.)
- **URLs reaching git.** Every repo/index URL is scheme-validated by one definition and every git invocation passes `--` before positionals. Repo URLs are attacker-influenced (index entries, `--index`, env), and git reads an option-shaped positional as an option — `--upload-pack`'s value is shell-interpreted.
- **The trust root is not repo-choosable.** The index URL cannot be set from committed settings; see below.
- **Names.** The installed name comes from the remote, so callers that already committed to a name pass it as a required argument and a mismatch is fatal.
- **Credentials.** Userinfo and query strings are stripped from every URL before printing, logging, or persisting (`.entire/logs/` is inside the working tree and `doctor bundle` collects it wholesale; `manifest.yml` is mode 0644).

Not claimed: **authenticity**. `checksums.txt` shares an origin with the asset, so it proves integrity in transit, not publisher identity. Real authenticity needs signatures.

## Design notes

- Built on the recorded founding decisions of this layer: PATH dispatch unchanged, built-ins win, `agent-` prefix reserved, env filtering untouched, no new telemetry.
- The only forge-specific code is the download-URL convention table; version listing, metadata, and the index all ride on the git protocol. No `go-github`-class dependency (uses existing `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` + `golang.org/x/mod`).
- **The plugin layer reads no settings at all.** The `settings` package is byte-identical to `main`.

## Changed since this description was first written

The branch was reviewed (Bugbot ×5 rounds, Copilot, four trail agent reviews, and a three-agent adversarial pass), then merged with `main` (2053 commits). Reviewers should know these are new:

**Behavior changes**
1. Checksums are now **required** by default (`--allow-unverified` opts out). Previously a release without them installed silently.
2. `http://` and `git://` are no longer accepted for repo or index URLs — unauthenticated transports, and the catalog decides what installs without a prompt.
3. Prereleases are excluded from tag resolution. `v2.0.0-rc1` outranks stable `v1.9.0` in semver, so `upgrade --all` was migrating users onto release candidates.

**Removals**
4. **`plugins.index_url` and `plugins.index_ttl_hours` are gone.** `.entire/settings.json` is committed and resolved from the working directory, while an index-listed plugin installs with *no prompt* — so a cloned repo could redirect the catalog and get an attacker-chosen binary onto `PATH` silently. The setting's value was that contributors got a different catalog *without knowing*, which is the vulnerability stated as a feature. Internal catalogs now use `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL`, which applies across repos and cannot be chosen by checked-out content. Go takes the same position with `GOPROXY`; npm's per-project registry is the cautionary counter-example.
5. **`requires[].repo_url` is gone.** Dependencies resolve by name through the index, so a dependency's URL comes from the curated catalog rather than the requiring plugin's author — planning contacted that URL *before* the confirmation prompt. A user can still install an out-of-catalog dependency themselves, with the usual prompt; the authority moved to the user.

**Fixes worth naming**
6. Argument injection into the git CLI allowing arbitrary command execution from a malicious index entry or dependency URL — verified live on the pre-fix tree, on a path that never prompts.
7. `entire-plugin.yml` now decodes **leniently**. Strict decoding meant the first author to adopt any future field would break installs on every older CLI, permanently. This is also what made removals 4 and 5 migration-free for already-published files.
8. Silent truncation of archive entries over 512 MiB, index-cache races (now flock-guarded), a diamond `min_version` skip, `darwin_all` universal binaries never matching, empty `entire-plugin.yml` being fatal, `index_ttl_hours` overflowing to "always stale", and credential leaks through download errors.

## Testing

- ~60 unit tests against `file://` git repos and `httptest` asset servers (zero real network in CI), covering tag resolution, asset selection/verification, extraction guards, index sync/TTL/offline/concurrency, dependency planning, doctor.
- 4 integration tests drive the spawned binary end to end: bare-name install → real dispatch → dependency install → remove guard → doctor exit code. They run the **verified** path — no test passes `--allow-unverified`, so their passing is the proof that verification succeeds.
- Security regressions assert the stronger property where it matters: that an injected payload never executes and that credentials never appear, not merely that a call errors. Each was verified RED against the pre-fix tree.
- `mise run check` green (fmt, lint, unit + integration + Vogon canary).

## Docs

- `docs/architecture/external-commands.md` — remote install, plugin index, dependencies, and the trust-boundary sections.
- README — user-facing Plugins section.

## Open, deliberately

- `browse` and `index.json`'s `platforms` are candidates to cut — `browse` adds no capability over `search` + `install` and installs unprompted; `platforms` warns but never enforces.
- `min_version` is not enforced on the install *outcome* (the planner computes a constraint nothing downstream checks), and dependencies have no `auto_installed` marker, so orphans leak.
- Two notions of "official": the `officialPlugins` telemetry allowlist and `index.json`'s `official` flag.
- `entire upgrade` (the self-update plugin) vs `entire plugin upgrade` (plugins).
- Follow-up outside this branch: a credential-redaction pass at `main.go`'s error print. `%w`-wrapped `url.Error` leaks the full URL regardless of call-site discipline, because `net/url.Error.Error()` does no redaction.
- Outside this repo: `graph` should be added to `entireio/plugin-index`, or `entire plugin install brain` reports its dependency as unindexed.

1	## Summary
2	
3	Expands the kubectl-style external-command layer so users can discover and install plugins without cloning anything, from any git host. 18 files, ~5,540 insertions.
4	
5	- **Remote install** — `entire plugin install <name|url|path>`. Newest **stable** semver tag via `git ls-remote` (forge-agnostic, inherits git auth and proxies; no forge REST client anywhere). Optional `entire-plugin.yml` metadata read via blobless shallow clone. Release assets download over HTTPS through a small per-host URL convention table (GitHub/Gitea-style, GitLab-style, `download_url` template escape hatch), selected and verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. Binaries land in `pkg/<name>/` with a provenance `manifest.yml`; `bin/` stays the only dispatch surface and the resolver in `plugin.go` is untouched.
6	- **Upgrade** — `entire plugin upgrade [name|--all]`, `--pin` to hold a tag, next-highest-tag fallback for pushed-but-unpublished releases, Windows locked-binary rename-aside.
7	- **Discovery** — krew-style git-synced index ([entireio/plugin-index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index)): shallow-cloned into the user cache keyed by URL hash, flock-guarded, 24h TTL, stale-copy-on-offline. Six new subcommands (`upgrade`, `search`, `info`, `browse`, `doctor`, `index update`) join the pre-existing `install`/`list`/`remove`; bare-name installs resolve through the index. Index URL: `--index` > `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` > built-in default.
8	- **Dependencies** — `entire-plugin.yml` `requires` (`name` + optional `min_version`, no ranges), resolved by name through the index. Install-time transitive planning, apt-style single confirmation, remove guard for depended-on plugins, and `entire plugin doctor`. Dispatch stays zero-cost — no runtime dependency checks.
9	
10	## Security model
11	
12	This code ends in downloading a binary and making it executable, so the trust boundaries are the design:
13	
14	- **Transport.** HTTPS required for anything off-machine, re-validated on every redirect hop (Go follows redirects across schemes; validating only the entry point is bypassable). Loopback exempt so `httptest` fixtures work.
15	- **Authentication.** A release that publishes no `checksums.txt` for the platform is **refused by default**; `--allow-unverified` opts in, is recorded in the manifest, reported by `doctor`, and inherited by `upgrade`.
16	- **Integrity.** The installed binary's digest is recorded as `binary_sha256` and re-checked by `doctor`. (`sha256` covers the downloaded *asset*, which is discarded with the staging dir — provenance only.)
17	- **URLs reaching git.** Every repo/index URL is scheme-validated by one definition and every git invocation passes `--` before positionals. Repo URLs are attacker-influenced (index entries, `--index`, env), and git reads an option-shaped positional as an option — `--upload-pack`'s value is shell-interpreted.
18	- **The trust root is not repo-choosable.** The index URL cannot be set from committed settings; see below.
19	- **Names.** The installed name comes from the remote, so callers that already committed to a name pass it as a required argument and a mismatch is fatal.
20	- **Credentials.** Userinfo and query strings are stripped from every URL before printing, logging, or persisting (`.entire/logs/` is inside the working tree and `doctor bundle` collects it wholesale; `manifest.yml` is mode 0644).
21	
22	Not claimed: **authenticity**. `checksums.txt` shares an origin with the asset, so it proves integrity in transit, not publisher identity. Real authenticity needs signatures.
23	
24	## Design notes
25	
26	- Built on the recorded founding decisions of this layer: PATH dispatch unchanged, built-ins win, `agent-` prefix reserved, env filtering untouched, no new telemetry.
27	- The only forge-specific code is the download-URL convention table; version listing, metadata, and the index all ride on the git protocol. No `go-github`-class dependency (uses existing `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` + `golang.org/x/mod`).
28	- **The plugin layer reads no settings at all.** The `settings` package is byte-identical to `main`.
29	
30	## Changed since this description was first written
31	
32	The branch was reviewed (Bugbot ×5 rounds, Copilot, four trail agent reviews, and a three-agent adversarial pass), then merged with `main` (2053 commits). Reviewers should know these are new:
33	
34	**Behavior changes**
35	1. Checksums are now **required** by default (`--allow-unverified` opts out). Previously a release without them installed silently.
36	2. `http://` and `git://` are no longer accepted for repo or index URLs — unauthenticated transports, and the catalog decides what installs without a prompt.
37	3. Prereleases are excluded from tag resolution. `v2.0.0-rc1` outranks stable `v1.9.0` in semver, so `upgrade --all` was migrating users onto release candidates.
38	
39	**Removals**
40	4. **`plugins.index_url` and `plugins.index_ttl_hours` are gone.** `.entire/settings.json` is committed and resolved from the working directory, while an index-listed plugin installs with *no prompt* — so a cloned repo could redirect the catalog and get an attacker-chosen binary onto `PATH` silently. The setting's value was that contributors got a different catalog *without knowing*, which is the vulnerability stated as a feature. Internal catalogs now use `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL`, which applies across repos and cannot be chosen by checked-out content. 46	8. 47	
48	## Testing
49	
50	- 77 unit tests against `file://` git repos and `httptest` asset servers (zero real network in CI), covering tag resolution, asset selection/verification, extraction guards, index sync/TTL/offline/concurrency, dependency planning, doctor.

53	- `mise run check` green (fmt, lint, unit + integration + Vogon canary).

The plugin layer reads no settings at all.

content.text:
Real bug, and mine. Fixed in `f4a5f206c` — CI green, lint 0 issues, finding resolved.

## What it was

`classifyInstallArg` tested for a literal `git@` prefix, while the `scpLikeGitURL` regex I added later accepts **any** SSH username. Two definitions of "scp-like git URL" that disagreed — and since the broader one came second, the classifier was the one left behind.

Anyone whose forge uses a non-default user hit this. Verified against the built binary before touching anything:

```
git@git.corp.io:group/entire-foo.git      → list tags of git@... : git ls-remote   ✓ routed to the repo
deploy@git.corp.io:group/entire-foo.git   → stat source: stat /tmp/deploy@git.corp.io:group/entire-foo.git:
                                             no such file or directory              ✗ routed to the filesystem
```

The second form is one my own validator would have happily installed from — the classifier just never let it get there. `deploy@`, `ci-bot@`, `forge-user@` are all ordinary in corporate SSH setups.

## The fix

`classifyInstallArg` now uses `scpLikeGitURL`, so there's one definition. The scp-like test has to run **before** the separator test, because these URLs contain a `/` too — which is exactly why the old ordering worked for `git@` (caught by the prefix check first) and failed for everything else.

After:
```
git@git.corp.io:...      → git ls-remote   ✓
deploy@git.corp.io:...   → git ls-remote   ✓
./entire-localdemo       → Installed plugin "localdemo" → …/bin/entire-localdemo   ✓
```

Test cases cover a non-default username, a hyphenated one, and `./deploy@host:x` — which stays a *path*, because the regex anchors the username at the start.

## Why this one is worth noting

It's the second finding of exactly this shape: I broadened a definition and left its twin behind. The first was `validatePluginRepoURL` vs `PluginSettings.Validate` disagreeing on `http://`/`git://`/absolute paths, which `/simplify` caught. Both times the fix was "one definition, shared" — and both times the drift came from *my* change rather than the original code.

Worth telling Thomas as a pattern, not just two bugs: `scpLikeGitURL` is now referenced from two places, so the next person to touch it should check both. There's an argument for the classifier and the validator living next to each other rather than in `plugin_group.go` and `plugin_gitremote.go`, though I'd leave that call to him.

The gates now read **Checks ✅ / Findings ✅**, with only the human-approval gate outstanding.

content.text:
Two things worth knowing before I answer:

```
classifyInstallArg    defined plugin_group.go
validatePluginRepoURL defined plugin_gitremote.go   used in 3 files
scpLikeGitURL         defined plugin_gitremote.go   used in 2 files
normalizeRepoURL      defined plugin_index.go
pluginNameFromRepoURL defined plugin_gitremote.go
releaseAssetBaseURL   defined plugin_fetch.go
```

The source-URL vocabulary is spread across **four** files, not two. And more importantly:

```
133:  if classifyInstallArg(arg) == installFromPath  { ... }   ← install RunE
182:  if classifyInstallArg(arg) == installFromIndex { ... }   ← runRemoteInstall
```

**The argument is classified twice.** That's the actual structural problem, and it's why the drift was easy to miss — the decision isn't made once and carried, it's re-derived from a raw string at each point of use. Co-locating files wouldn't have prevented it.

## What I'd suggest

**Make it one decision, not two.** A `parseInstallSource` that classifies *and* validates in a single pass, called once at the command boundary, with a typed result passed down:

```go
type installSource struct {
    Kind installArgKind
    // Ref is the repository URL, the filesystem path, or the catalog name,
    // according to Kind.
    Ref string
}

func parseInstallSource(arg string) (installSource, error) {
    switch {
    case strings.Contains(arg, "://") || scpLikeGitURL.MatchString(arg):
        return installSource{installFromURL, arg}, validatePluginRepoURL(arg)
    case strings.ContainsAny(arg, `/\`) || strings.HasPrefix(arg, "."):
        return installSource{installFromPath, arg}, nil
    default:
        return installSource{installFromIndex, arg}, validatePluginName(arg)
    }
}
```

Why this rather than co-location:

- **Classification and validation can't disagree** — they're the same function. The bug I just fixed becomes unrepresentable rather than merely commented.
- **The arg is classified once.** `runRemoteInstall` takes a typed source instead of re-deriving from a string.
- **It's a free error-message upgrade.** A bare name currently goes to the index and comes back "not in the index"; validating at the boundary means `agent-foo` says "reserved prefix" and a name with a separator says so, instead of blaming the catalog.

Cost is small — one type, one function, two call sites rewired, all in files already in the diff. And the justification isn't aesthetic: this exact 3-way switch has already drifted once and is already evaluated twice.

**Then, and only then, a `plugin_source.go`** holding `installArgKind`, `installSource`, `parseInstallSource`, `validatePluginRepoURL`, `gitURLSchemes`, `scpLikeGitURL`, `normalizeRepoURL`, `pluginNameFromRepoURL`. That's a coherent unit — "what is a plugin source, and what can you ask about one" — and it leaves `plugin_gitremote.go` as what its name says: the git shell-outs. But this is secondary. Co-location makes the next drift *visible*; the single decision makes it *impossible*. Do the second first.

**What I would not move:** `releaseAssetBaseURL` and `requireSecureAssetURL` stay in `plugin_fetch.go`. They're about asset URLs and download transport, a genuinely different concern from "what did the user ask to install."

## The honest counter

You could argue a type and a function is heavy for a three-way switch on a string. I don't think so here, but the reason is empirical rather than principled: it drifted once already, and it's computed twice. Absent that evidence I'd have left it alone.

This is small and mechanical enough that I'd just do it rather than route it to Thomas — the `plugin_source.go` move is the part I'd leave to him, since file layout is more taste than correctness. Want me to do the `parseInstallSource` half?

content.text:
Done — `32991c49a`. Full CI green, lint 0 issues.

## What landed

`parseInstallSource(arg) (installSource, error)` classifies and validates in one pass, called once at the command boundary. `runRemoteInstall` now takes a typed `installSource` instead of re-deriving the kind from a raw string.

Three things fell out of it:

**The drift is now unrepresentable.** One function can't disagree with itself. Sharing the regex fixed the bug; this removes the shape that produced it.

**The argument is classified once.** It was being classified twice — once in the install command to split off the path case, once in `runRemoteInstall` for the index case.

**Better errors, for free.** `entire plugin install agent-evil` now says `plugin name "agent-evil" is reserved for the external agent protocol` instead of going to the catalog and coming back "not in the index".

I also added a leading-`-` rejection for every kind. Previously `--upload-pack=touch /tmp/x; git-upload-pack` contained a separator, so it went down the *path* branch and failed as `stat: no such file` — safe, but a confusing way to say "that's not a plugin."

## Two things my own test got wrong

Worth recording, because the failures were informative rather than annoying. I wrote expectations that `--upload-pack=…` and `ext::sh -c whoami` would be rejected as URLs. Neither was:

- `--upload-pack=…` contains `/`, so it was a *path*
- `ext::sh -c whoami` has no separator and no scheme, so it was an *index name* — and `validatePluginName` permits spaces and colons

The code was right and my mental model was wrong. Both stop well before git sees a repository URL, which is the property that actually matters. I fixed the expectations rather than the code, and left a comment recording why those two shapes are deliberately accepted — otherwise the next person reads the gap as an oversight and "fixes" it.

I did **not** tighten `validatePluginName` to reject spaces and colons. It's pre-existing, it also governs local installs, and the looseness is harmless on the two routes that reach it.

## The file-layout half

Not done, deliberately, and the commit message says so. The source vocabulary is spread over four files — validator and scp regex in `plugin_gitremote.go`, the parser in `plugin_group.go`, `normalizeRepoURL` in `plugin_index.go`, asset URLs in `plugin_fetch.go`. Co-location would make a future drift *visible*; one decision makes it *impossible*. Having done the second, the first is now optional taste rather than risk mitigation — which is why it's a reasonable thing to leave to Thomas rather than something I should have pushed through.

Trail gates read **Checks ✅ / Findings ✅**, human approval still the only thing outstanding.

2	
3	Expands the kubectl-style external-command layer so users can discover and install plugins without cloning anything, from any git host. 18 files, ~5,540 insertions.
4	
5	- **Remote install** — `entire plugin install <name|url|path>`. Newest **stable** semver tag via `git ls-remote` (forge-agnostic, inherits git auth and proxies; no forge REST client anywhere). Release assets download over HTTPS through a small per-host URL convention table (GitHub/Gitea-style, GitLab-style, `download_url` template escape hatch), selected and verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. Binaries land in `pkg/<name>/` with a provenance `manifest.yml`; `bin/` stays the only dispatch surface and the resolver in `plugin.go` is untouched.
6	- **Upgrade** — `entire plugin upgrade [name|--all]`, `--pin` to hold a tag, next-highest-tag fallback for pushed-but-unpublished releases, Windows locked-binary rename-aside.
7	- **Discovery** — krew-style git-synced index ([entireio/plugin-index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index)): shallow-cloned into the user cache keyed by URL hash, flock-guarded, 24h TTL, stale-copy-on-offline. Six new subcommands (`upgrade`, `search`, `info`, `browse`, `doctor`, `index update`) join the pre-existing `install`/`list`/`remove`; bare-name installs resolve through the index. Index URL: `--index` > `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` > built-in default.
8	- **Dependencies** — `entire-plugin.yml` `requires` (`name` + optional `min_version`, no ranges), resolved by name through the index. Install-time transitive planning, apt-style single confirmation, remove guard for depended-on plugins, and `entire plugin doctor`. Dispatch stays zero-cost — no runtime dependency checks.
9	
10	## Security model
11	
12	This code ends in downloading a binary and making it executable, so the trust boundaries are the design:
13	
14	- **Transport.** HTTPS required for anything off-machine, re-validated on every redirect hop (Go follows redirects across schemes; validating only the entry point is bypassable). Loopback exempt so `httptest` fixtures work.
15	- **Authentication.** A release that publishes no `checksums.txt` for the platform is **refused by default**; `--allow-unverified` opts in, is recorded in the manifest, reported by `doctor`, and inherited by `upgrade`.
16	- **Integrity.** The installed binary's digest is recorded as `binary_sha256` and re-checked by `doctor`. (`sha256` covers the downloaded *asset*, which is discarded with the staging dir — provenance only.)
17	- **URLs reaching git.** Every repo/index URL is scheme-validated by one definition and every git invocation passes `--` before positionals. Repo URLs are attacker-influenced (index entries, `--index`, env), and git reads an option-shaped positional as an option — `--upload-pack`'s value is shell-interpreted.
18	- **The trust root is not repo-choosable.** The index URL cannot be set from committed settings; see below.
19	- **Names.** The installed name comes from the remote, so callers that already committed to a name pass it as a required argument and a mismatch is fatal.
20	- **Credentials.** Userinfo and query strings are stripped from every URL before printing, logging, or persisting (`.entire/logs/` is inside the working tree and `doctor bundle` collects it wholesale; `manifest.yml` is mode 0644).
21	
22	Not claimed: **authenticity**. `checksums.txt` shares an origin with the asset, so it proves integrity in transit, not publisher identity. Real authenticity needs signatures.
23	
24	## Design notes
25	
26	- Built on the recorded founding decisions of this layer: PATH dispatch unchanged, built-ins win, `agent-` prefix reserved, env filtering untouched, no new telemetry.
27	- The only forge-specific code is the download-URL convention table; version listing, metadata, and the index all ride on the git protocol. No `go-github`-class dependency (uses existing `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` + `golang.org/x/mod`).
28	- **The plugin layer reads no settings at all.** The `settings` package is byte-identical to `main`.
29	
30	## Changed since this description was first written
31	
32	The branch was reviewed (Bugbot ×5 rounds, Copilot, four trail agent reviews, and a three-agent adversarial pass), then merged with `main` (2053 commits). Reviewers should know these are new:
33	
34	**Behavior changes**
35	1. Checksums are now **required** by default (`--allow-unverified` opts out). Previously a release without them installed silently.
36	2. `http://` and `git://` are no longer accepted for repo or index URLs — unauthenticated transports, and the catalog decides what installs without a prompt.
37	3. Prereleases are excluded from tag resolution. `v2.0.0-rc1` outranks stable `v1.9.0` in semver, so `upgrade --all` was migrating users onto release candidates.
38	
39	**Removals**
40	4. **`plugins.index_url` and `plugins.index_ttl_hours` are gone.** `.entire/settings.json` is committed and resolved from the working directory, while an index-listed plugin installs with *no prompt* — so a cloned repo could redirect the catalog and get an attacker-chosen binary onto `PATH` silently. The setting's value was that contributors got a different catalog *without knowing*, which is the vulnerability stated as a feature. Internal catalogs now use `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL`, which applies across repos and cannot be chosen by checked-out content. Go takes the same position with `GOPROXY`; npm's per-project registry is the cautionary counter-example.
41	5. **`requires[].repo_url` is gone.** Dependencies resolve by name through the index, so a dependency's URL comes from the curated catalog rather than the requiring plugin's author — planning contacted that URL *before* the confirmation prompt. A user can still install an out-of-catalog dependency themselves, with the usual prompt; the authority moved to the user.
42	
43	**Fixes worth naming**
44	6. Argument injection into the git CLI allowing arbitrary command execution from a malicious index entry or dependency URL — verified live on the pre-fix tree, on a path that never prompts.
45	7. `entire-plugin.yml` now decodes **leniently**. Strict decoding meant the first author to adopt any future field would break installs on every older CLI, permanently. This is also what made removals 4 and 5 migration-free for already-published files.
46	8. Silent truncation of archive entries over 512 MiB, index-cache races (now flock-guarded), a diamond `min_version` skip, `darwin_all` universal binaries never matching, empty `entire-plugin.yml` being fatal, `index_ttl_hours` overflowing to "always stale", and credential leaks through download errors.

48	## Testing
49	
50	- 77 unit tests against `file://` git repos and `httptest` asset servers (zero real network in CI), covering tag resolution, asset selection/verification, extraction guards, index sync/TTL/offline/concurrency, dependency planning, doctor.
51	- 4 integration tests drive the spawned binary end to end (install/dispatch, unlisted-URL gating, dependencies + remove guard, search/info): bare-name install → real dispatch → dependency install → remove guard → doctor exit code. They run the **verified** path — no test passes `--allow-unverified`, so their passing is the proof that verification succeeds.
52	- Security regressions assert the stronger property where it matters: that an injected payload never executes and that credentials never appear, not merely that a call errors. Each was verified RED against the pre-fix tree.
53	- `mise run check` green (fmt, lint, unit + integration + Vogon canary).
54	
55	## Docs
56	
57	- `docs/architecture/external-commands.md` — remote install, plugin index, dependencies, and the trust-boundary sections.
58	- README — user-facing Plugins section.

61	
62	- `browse` and `index.json`'s `platforms` are candidates to cut — `browse` adds no capability over `search` + `install` and installs unprompted; `platforms` warns but never enforces.

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"os/exec"
7		"path/filepath"
8		"runtime"
9		"slices"
10		"strings"
11	
12		"golang.org/x/mod/semver"
13	)
14	
15	// Dependency handling is install-time only. Dispatch stays zero-cost: a
16	// plugin invokes its deps as entire-<dep> via PATH at runtime (the managed
17	// bin dir is prepended for plugin children), and `entire plugin doctor`
18	// reports drift after the fact. There is deliberately no version-range
19	// solver — requirements carry at most a minimum version.
20	
21	// maxDepDepth bounds transitive resolution. Plugin graphs are shallow in
22	// practice; the bound turns a metadata cycle that slips past the visited
23	// set (e.g. two names aliasing one repo) into an error instead of a hang.
24	const maxDepDepth = 10
25	
26	// DepAction is one planned dependency install or upgrade.
27	type DepAction struct {
28		Name       string
29		RepoURL    string
30		MinVersion string
31		// Upgrade is true when the dependency is installed but below
32		// MinVersion; the action reinstalls at the latest tag.
33		Upgrade bool
34		// CurrentTag is the installed tag for upgrades.
35		CurrentTag string
36	}
37	
38	// DepPlan is the result of resolving a plugin's transitive requirements.
39	type DepPlan struct {
40		Actions []DepAction
41		// Warnings are non-blocking observations, e.g. a dependency satisfied
42		// from raw $PATH whose version cannot be verified.
43		Warnings []string
44	}
45	
46	// PlanDependencyInstalls resolves the transitive requirements of rootReqs
47	// into ordered install/upgrade actions. Missing dependencies must be
48	// resolvable to a repo URL via the requirement itself or the index. The
49	// visited set plus a depth bound make cycles an error path, not a hang.
50	func PlanDependencyInstalls(ctx context.Context, rootReqs []PluginRequirement, idx *PluginIndex) (*DepPlan, error) {
51		plan := &DepPlan{}
52		// name -> strictest min_version considered so far, not a plain seen-set:
53		// see planDeps.
54		considered := map[string]string{}
55		if err := planDeps(ctx, rootReqs, idx, plan, considered, 0); err != nil {
56			return nil, err
57		}
58		return plan, nil
59	}
60	
61	// stricterMinVersion reports whether a demands a higher minimum than b.
62	// An empty string means "no minimum": nothing is stricter than it, and any
63	// concrete minimum is stricter than it.
64	func stricterMinVersion(a, b string) bool {
65		switch {
66		case a == "":
67			return false
68		case b == "":
69			return true
70		default:
71			return semver.Compare(canonicalSemver(a), canonicalSemver(b)) > 0
72		}
73	}
74	
75	// upsertDepAction keeps one action per plugin name, replacing an earlier
76	// entry when a stricter requirement supersedes it.
77	func upsertDepAction(plan *DepPlan, action DepAction) {
78		for i := range plan.Actions {
79			if plan.Actions[i].Name == action.Name {
80				plan.Actions[i] = action
81				return
82			}
83		}
84		plan.Actions = append(plan.Actions, action)
85	}
86	
87	// addDepWarning appends a warning unless it is already present. Re-visiting a
88	// name under a stricter constraint can re-derive the same observation, and
89	// printing it twice would just look like a bug.
90	func addDepWarning(plan *DepPlan, warning string) {
91		if warning == "" || slices.Contains(plan.Warnings, warning) {
92			return
93		}
94		plan.Warnings = append(plan.Warnings, warning)
95	}
96	
97	func planDeps(ctx context.Context, reqs []PluginRequirement, idx *PluginIndex, plan *DepPlan, considered map[string]string, depth int) error {
98		if depth > maxDepDepth {
99			return fmt.Errorf("dependency chain deeper than %d; cycle in plugin metadata?", maxDepDepth)
100		}
101		for _, req := range reqs {
102			// Keyed by name *and* gated on the strictest min_version seen so far,
103			// not a plain seen-set. In a diamond where two requirers demand
104			// different minimums of the same plugin (A needs C >= v1, B needs
105			// C >= v2), a name-only set skipped B's stricter constraint entirely:
106			// an installed C satisfying v1 produced no action and no warning, so
107			// the install completed leaving B running against a too-old C. Doctor
108			// caught it afterwards — it walks each manifest's requirements
109			// independently — but the install should plan the upgrade, not defer
110			// the discovery.
111			if prev, seen := considered[req.Name]; seen && !stricterMinVersion(req.MinVersion, prev) {
112				continue

114			// Past the guard this name is either new or strictly stricter than
115			// what was recorded, so this requirement's minimum is the one to keep.
116			considered[req.Name] = req.MinVersion
117	
118			status, err := dependencySatisfied(req)
119			if err != nil {
120				return err
121			}
122			addDepWarning(plan, status.Warning)
123			if status.Satisfied {
124				// An already-satisfied managed dependency can itself have
125				// gaps (e.g. its own dep was removed with --force since
126				// install). Walk its recorded requirements — offline, from
127				// the manifest — so installing a parent repairs the whole
128				// chain instead of stopping at the first satisfied node.
129				// PATH/local-dev installs have no manifest; doctor covers
130				// those.
131				if status.Manifest != nil {
132					if err := planDeps(ctx, status.Manifest.Requires, idx, plan, considered, depth+1); err != nil {
133						return err
134					}
135				}
136				continue
137			}
138	
139			action := DepAction{Name: req.Name, MinVersion: req.MinVersion}
140			if m := status.Manifest; m != nil {

142				// recorded repo.
143				action.Upgrade = true

148				// source. See PluginRequirement for why an author-supplied URL is

154				action.RepoURL = e.RepoURL
155			}
156			upsertDepAction(plan, action)

158			// Recurse into what the dependency itself requires, using metadata
159			// only — nothing is downloaded during planning. Inspection
160			// failures don't fail the plan (the install will surface hard
161			// errors itself), but they must not be silent either: a confirmed
162			// plan that quietly omitted nested dependencies would look
163			// complete while leaving gaps for doctor to find.
164			tag := ""
165			if tags, err := listRemoteSemverTags(ctx, action.RepoURL); err == nil && len(tags) > 0 {
166				tag = tags[0]
167			}
168			if tag == "" {
169				addDepWarning(plan, fmt.Sprintf("could not list tags for %q (%s); its own dependencies were not inspected — 'entire plugin doctor' will report any gaps", req.Name, redactURL(action.RepoURL)))

171			}

176			}
177			if meta == nil {
178				continue // no metadata file: no declared dependencies
179			}
180			if err := planDeps(ctx, meta.Requires, idx, plan, considered, depth+1); err != nil {
181				return err
182			}
183		}
184		return nil
185	}

1	# External Commands
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	The Entire CLI supports kubectl-style external commands — standalone binaries on `$PATH` that extend the CLI without modifying the main repository. When the user invokes `entire <name>` and `<name>` isn't a built-in subcommand, the CLI looks for an `entire-<name>` binary on `$PATH` and execs it with the remaining arguments. Stdio passes through, exit codes propagate, and the parent CLI does no further processing of the child's output.
6	
7	This is **not** the same mechanism as the [external agent protocol](external-agent-protocol.md). External commands have no protocol, no JSON contract, no lifecycle hooks. Use the agent protocol when you need checkpoint integration; use external commands for everything else.
8	
9	## Resolution
10	
11	The CLI does not scan `$PATH` at startup. Resolution is lazy: when `os.Args[1]` doesn't match a built-in subcommand, the CLI calls `exec.LookPath("entire-" + os.Args[1])`. If a binary is found and executable, it runs before Cobra parses arguments.
12	
13	Rules, in order:
14	
15	1. **Built-ins win.** If the first argument matches a Cobra subcommand (or one of its aliases), the external command is never considered.
16	2. **Reserved names are skipped.** Names beginning with `agent-` are reserved for the [agent protocol](external-agent-protocol.md). The resolver refuses to invoke them as external commands.
17	3. **Path-traversal candidates are rejected.** Names containing `/` or `\` never resolve.
18	4. **Found-but-not-executable surfaces as a launch error.** If `entire-<name>` exists on `$PATH` but lacks the executable bit, the resolver reports `Failed to run plugin entire-<name>` with exit code 1, rather than falling through to Cobra's "unknown command" path.
19	
20	### Managed install directory
21	
22	Users can drop binaries anywhere on `$PATH`, but a per-user managed directory is also automatically discovered:
23	
24	- **Default:** `$XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins/bin` (Linux/macOS) or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\entire\plugins\bin` (Windows).
25	- **Override:** `$ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR/bin`.
26	
27	The CLI prepends this directory to `$PATH` at startup via `cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH()` so the existing `exec.LookPath` resolution finds managed installs without any special-casing. This is purely additive — the kubectl-style `$PATH` model is unchanged.
28	
29	`entire plugin install/list/remove/upgrade` manage the contents of this directory. Authors who prefer the raw "drop a binary on `$PATH`" model don't need to use it.
30	
31	### Remote install
32	
33	`entire plugin install` accepts three source forms:
34	
35	| Form | Example | Behavior |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| bare name | `entire plugin install run` | Resolved through the [plugin index](#plugin-index-discovery) |
38	| repository URL | `entire plugin install https://github.com/entireio/entire-run` | Installs from any git host. Also accepts git's scp-like form with any SSH username (`deploy@git.corp.io:group/entire-foo.git`) — the same set `validatePluginRepoURL` allows |
39	| local path | `entire plugin install ./dist/entire-run` | Symlink/copy into the managed dir (unchanged) |
40	
41	Remote installs are deliberately forge-agnostic:
42	
43	1. **Version resolution** uses `git ls-remote --tags` — identical on GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, and self-hosted servers; inherits the user's git auth and proxy config. The highest **stable** semver tag wins; `--pin <tag>` installs exactly that tag and marks the manifest pinned (skipped by `upgrade`).
44	
45	   Prereleases are excluded from resolution. semver ranks `v2.0.0-rc1` above stable `v1.9.0`, so listing them would move every user onto a release candidate on the next `plugin upgrade --all` the moment an author pushed one. `--pin` is the opt-in, since it bypasses listing entirely. Every git subprocess also carries a two-minute deadline — the root context is cancellable but has no timeout, so an unreachable host would otherwise hang the command with no output, which matters most during dependency planning against author-controlled URLs.
46	2. **Metadata** is read from `entire-plugin.yml` at the repo root via a blobless shallow clone (with a plain shallow-clone fallback for servers that don't allow partial-clone filters). The file is optional; without it the plugin name derives from the repo basename (`entire-run` → `run`).
47	3. **Asset download** is the one forge-specific step, contained in a small URL-convention table: GitHub/Gitea-style `<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>`, GitLab-style `<repo>/-/releases/<tag>/downloads/<asset>`, unknown hosts default to GitHub-style. Authors on other hosts declare a `download_url` template in `entire-plugin.yml` (placeholders: `{name}` `{tag}` `{version}` `{os}` `{arch}` `{asset}`).
48	4. **Asset selection** goes through the release's `checksums.txt`: the manifest lists what was actually published, and the download is verified against it. Candidate names follow goreleaser conventions (`entire-<name>_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` and friends, with `x86_64`/`aarch64` aliases and a `darwin_all` universal-binary fallback (`all` occupies the *arch* slot, which is where goreleaser puts it)). A pushed tag with no published assets falls back to the next-highest tag with a warning.
49	5. The binary lands in `pkg/<name>/` next to a `manifest.yml` — written atomically, and *before* the `bin/` link — recording provenance (repo URL, tag, asset, asset SHA-256, **binary SHA-256**, verification state, pin state, dependency list), and is linked into `bin/` through the same symlink→hardlink→copy fallback as local installs. The dispatcher never changes.
50	
51	The manifest is written immediately after the binary swap and before the `bin/` link, which is ordering that matters rather than style. `replaceBinary` has already mutated `pkg/<name>/`; until the manifest catches up it records the *previous* tag and `binary_sha256` while the new binary is on disk, and `doctor`'s integrity check reads that as tampering — a permanent false alarm on a healthy install. Writing it first leaves only a local re-hash in that window, and if the link then fails, `doctor` reports the real problem ("has an install manifest but no entry in the managed bin dir") with a fix that works.
52	
53	The two digests are not redundant. `sha256` covers the downloaded asset, which is usually an archive and is discarded with the staging directory — provenance only, nothing left to compare against. `binary_sha256` covers the executable under `pkg/<name>/`, which is what `entire plugin doctor` re-hashes to detect a binary swapped out after install.
54	
55	Installing from a URL not listed in the index prints the source and asks for confirmation (`--yes` to skip; required in non-interactive runs). Index-listed repos install without prompting.
56	
57	#### Repository URLs are a security boundary
58	
59	Every repo URL is validated by `validatePluginRepoURL` before it reaches the git CLI, and every git invocation passes `--` before its positionals. Both layers exist because repo URLs are attacker-influenced: they arrive from `index.json` entries and from `--index`/`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL`.
60	
61	git parses an option-shaped positional as an option, and `--upload-pack=<cmd>` is shell-interpreted — with no positional repository left, it runs against the *ambient* repo's `origin`. So a catalog entry like `--upload-pack=curl … | sh; git-upload-pack` would execute arbitrary commands during an index-resolved install, which by design never prompts. Dependency planning is the tightest path: it contacts a dependency's repository — now always an index-listed one — *before* the install confirmation.
62	
63	Accepted forms are `https://`, `ssh://`, `file://`, and git's `user@host:path` scp-like syntax. Anything else — a leading `-`, a bare name, a relative or bare absolute path, git's command-executing `ext::` transport — is rejected.
64

git add -A && git commit -q --no-verify -F - <<'MSG'
Keep the manifest consistent with the binary, and verify dependency outcomes

Two findings from the agent review of the current head.

The manifest is now written immediately after the binary swap, before the bin/
link. replaceBinary has already mutated pkg/<name>/ by that point, and until the
manifest catches up it records the *previous* tag and binary_sha256 while the new
binary is on disk — which checkManagedBinaryIntegrity reads as tampering. A
failure or interrupt in any of the three steps that used to sit between the swap
and the manifest write left a permanent false "modified or replaced outside
entire" alarm on a perfectly good install, and a stale tag in `plugin list`.

Reordering leaves only the local re-hash in that window, and turns the remaining
failure mode into an accurate one: if the bin/ link then fails, the manifest is
correct and doctor reports "has an install manifest but no entry in the managed
bin dir" with a fix that works, instead of accusing the user of tampering.
SavePluginManifest also writes through jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic now, so a torn
manifest cannot be produced either — the same shared helper the settings and
checkpoint stores already use.

ExecuteDepPlan verifies the outcome rather than the attempt. It installs the
newest published tag, which may still be below the minimum the plan computed —
if a dependency hasn't cut a release meeting the parent's requirement, the loop
reported success and printed "Installed dependency", silently defeating the
guarantee PlanDependencyInstalls had just derived. It now fails with both
versions named. The check runs after the install, so the dependency is left on
disk at the too-old version: deliberate, because doctor then reports "requires
demo >= v9.0.0 but v0.1.0 is installed", which is accurate and actionable rather
than leaving nothing to diagnose.

This closes the min_version-enforcement gap that had been listed as knowingly
open since the dependency system was first reviewed.

content.text:
Both were still relevant, and both real. Fixed in `653eced31` — full CI green, lint 0 issues, both resolved.

## The seven older findings

All show `resolved / stale`. Stale means the code they point at has since moved — expected after this many refactors, and no action needed. Nothing was reintroduced.

## The two new ones

**Manifest inconsistent with the binary** (`plugin_install_remote.go:169`). Verified the ordering: `replaceBinary` ran, then `fileSHA256`, `InstallPluginFromPath`, and `SavePluginManifest` — three fallible steps *after* the binary was already swapped. A failure or Ctrl+C in any of them left the new binary on disk against the old recorded tag and digest, which `checkManagedBinaryIntegrity` reads as *"modified or replaced outside entire"*.

That's the worst kind of bug in a security feature: a **permanent false tampering alarm on a healthy install**. It teaches users to ignore the alarm.

The manifest now writes immediately after the swap, before the `bin/` link, leaving only a local re-hash in the window. And the residual failure mode became an accurate one — if the link fails, doctor says *"has an install manifest but no entry in the managed bin dir"* with a fix that works. `SavePluginManifest` also goes through `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic` now, which closes the reuse finding from `/simplify` at the same time.

**Dependency outcome unverified** (`plugin_deps.go:249`). `ExecuteDepPlan` installed the newest published tag and never checked it against the plan's `min_version`, so if a dependency hadn't cut a qualifying release it printed "Installed dependency" while the requirement stayed unmet. It now fails with both versions named.

This is the item that had been sitting on the knowingly-open list since the dependency system was first reviewed — I'd flagged it three times as "the price of keeping `requires[]`". It's now paid. The check runs *after* the install deliberately, so the dependency stays on disk at the too-old version and doctor reports `requires demo >= v9.0.0 but v0.1.0 is installed` — accurate and actionable, rather than leaving nothing to diagnose.

## Two bugs in my own tests, worth noting

Both first drafts failed for reasons that were about my tests, not the code:

- The dependency test's second case hit `already installed; use --force` — because the *first* case's install succeeds before the min-version check rejects it. That's the behavior I'd just designed, and I'd forgotten it one line later. Fixed with `Upgrade: true`, and I added an assertion documenting that the too-old version is deliberately left installed.
- The upgrade test called `updateRepoMetadata` with content identical to what was already committed → `cannot create empty commit`. A new tag on the same commit was all it needed.

Both are the kind of thing that would have been a confusing CI failure for someone else, so I'd rather they surfaced here.

## Remaining open

From the earlier reviews, all still open and all deliberate: `browse` and `platforms` as cut candidates, `auto_installed` orphan tracking, the two notions of "official", `entire upgrade` naming, the `main.go` redaction follow-up, and adding `graph` to the published index.

The min-version item has dropped off that list. Gates should read **Checks ✅ / Findings ✅** once CI finishes on this head.

content.text:
Both are small pieces of the discovery surface.

## `entire plugin browse`

An interactive picker over the catalog. It syncs the index, builds a `huh` select list of every entry as `name — description` plus a `(cancel)` option, and on selection calls `runRemoteInstall` with the chosen name.

```
$ entire plugin browse
? Install a plugin
  > run — Launch one of the agents enabled for Entire in the current repository
    upgrade — Upgrade the system-installed entire binary
    (cancel)
```

It needs a TTY — without one it errors and points at `search`.

**Why it's a cut candidate:** it's `search` + `install` with arrow keys, and it installs on **one keypress with no confirmation**. Index-resolved installs are treated as trusted and never prompt, so the select list *is* the confirmation — Enter on a highlighted row downloads a binary and puts it on your `PATH`. `search` then `install <name>` is two commands, but the second is a deliberate act. Combined with a catalog that currently has two entries, it's the piece I'd cut with least hesitation.

## `platforms` in `index.json`

An optional per-entry list of GOOS values — "supported platforms when the plugin doesn't ship the full matrix; empty means all":

```json
{"name": "run", "repo_url": "...", "platforms": ["darwin", "linux"]}
```

It's read in exactly two places. `plugin info` displays it, and on install it produces a warning that changes nothing:

```go
if len(entry.Platforms) > 0 && !slices.Contains(entry.Platforms, runtime.GOOS) {
    fmt.Fprintf(errOut, "Warning: index lists %q for %s only; this is %s — continuing anyway.\n", ...)
}
```

**Why it's a cut candidate — two reasons, and the second is the real one:**

It enforces nothing. If the platform genuinely isn't published, the download fails on its own a moment later with `no matching release asset for windows/amd64 at <repo> <tag>` — which is more accurate, since it reflects what was *actually* published rather than what the catalog claims.

And it lives in the wrong artifact. The **author** knows their build matrix; the **catalog** is a third party describing someone else's release. So it drifts in the direction that hurts: an author adds Windows support, the catalog entry still says `["darwin","linux"]`, and the CLI now warns about a plugin that works perfectly. A stale "this won't work" is worse than no claim at all.

If you wanted the capability, the right home is `entire-plugin.yml` alongside `download_url`, where it can't drift from the release. Even there it'd be largely redundant with asset probing.

## My recommendation on each

**`platforms`** — cut. There's no version of this that earns its place in the catalog, and the honest signal already exists in the download failure.

**`browse`** — cut, or keep it and add a confirmation. The no-prompt install is the part I'd object to more than the redundancy; a picker that shows the repo URL and asks before installing would be defensible. But given `search` already prints everything the picker shows, cutting is simpler.

Both are Thomas's calls — they're features he built, and neither is broken. They're "this costs more than it earns" arguments, not defect reports, which is why I've kept them on the list rather than acting on them.

Added in `fb8412b57`. Full CI green, lint 0 issues.

## What browse does now

```
$ entire plugin browse
? Install a plugin
  > run — Launch one of the agents enabled for Entire in the current repository
    upgrade — Upgrade the system-installed entire binary
    (cancel)

? Install "run" from https://github.com/entireio/entire-run?   ← new
```

The confirmation names **the repository**, which is the fact the picker hides — it only ever showed name and description. That's the substantive part: previously you could arrow to a row, press Enter, and a binary from a URL you'd never seen was downloaded and linked onto your `PATH`.

It follows the same `handleFormCancellation` convention as the untrusted-URL prompt, so Esc and "No" both exit cleanly with `Install cancelled.` rather than differing by exit code.

I also gave browse a `Long` description — it had only a one-line `Short` — stating that it needs a terminal and pointing at `search` + `install <name>`. That's the non-interactive equivalent the repo's agent-safe-fallback rule requires, and it was already the behavior; it just wasn't documented.

## On the test

Worth being straight about the limit: the interactive prompt itself isn't unit-testable without a TTY harness. Under `go test`, `CanPromptInteractively()` is false, so browse returns at its terminal check before the confirm is reachable.

So the test covers the documented no-terminal path and asserts the error names the alternative. That's the same coverage shape the untrusted-URL prompt has — `TestPluginRemoteInstall_URLNeedsYesWhenUnlisted` tests the non-interactive gate, not the prompt. I followed the existing pattern rather than inventing a harness for one call site, but the confirm logic itself is unexercised, and that's a real gap rather than something I've covered.

## What this does and doesn't settle

Here's the answer to both halves:

## PR comments — nothing new

The last comment is my own from Aug 5. No new bot reviews (Bugbot hasn't re-run), and **all 13 review threads are resolved**. Nothing is waiting on you there.

## Trail — one new Low finding, now fixed (`ab61a0b7e`)

`ParsePluginMetadata` validated each requirement's `name` but not its `min_version`. I verified the mechanism before touching it:

```
min="v0.2.0"  valid=true   Compare(v1.0.0,min)= 1  satisfied=true
min="vtypo"   valid=false  Compare(v1.0.0,min)= 1  satisfied=true   ←
min="latest"  valid=false  Compare(v1.0.0,min)= 1  satisfied=true   ←
min=">=1.0"   valid=false  Compare(v1.0.0,min)= 1  satisfied=true   ←
```

`x/mod/semver` ranks an invalid string below *every* valid one, so a typo doesn't fail — it makes the comparison always true and the version floor **silently disappears**. Low severity is right (it needs an author typo, and it weakens rather than breaks), but it's the worst failure direction for a guarantee: you'd believe the minimum was enforced when nothing was checking it.

The likeliest mistake is range syntax, since the field is deliberately a minimum only — and `>=1.0` is precisely one of the shapes that disabled the check. It now gets an explicit "minimum only — ranges are not supported."

## One thing I want to flag about this fix

It looks like it contradicts a decision I made earlier today. This morning I made `entire-plugin.yml` decode **leniently** and argued that author-side validation belongs in a lint command, not in every user's install path. Now I'm adding author-side validation to that same function.

The distinction is real, and I put it in the code comment so the next reader doesn't see a contradiction:

- **Unknown keys stay lenient** — they're a *newer CLI's fields*. Refusing them breaks older binaries permanently, for everyone on that version, with no way for the author to fix it.
- **A malformed value of a known field is strict** — no CLI version will ever accept `latest` as a semver tag. Rejecting it costs the author one confused test run.

And the precedent was already there: `req.Name` is validated in the very same loop. So this is consistent with that function's existing behavior, not a new policy.

## State

```
PR #1422 · head ab61a0b7e · MERGEABLE · all review threads resolved
No open trail findings · no new comments
```

The agent review will re-run on this head; I'll check again if you want. Six review rounds in, the findings have moved from RCE-class to "a typo weakens a check," which is a reasonable signal that the surface is getting thin — though it's also found something real every single round, so I wouldn't call it done.

id: 019fd8cf-e96c-77e8-a8c6-5a5b74a908ed | sev: medium
`cmd/entire/cli/plugin_group.go:281-284` — a URL install with an unreachable index hard-fails *after* the plugin is already installed, with a misleading message. `idx` is nil whenever `SyncPluginIndex` failed (offline, no cache): `trusted` short-circuits on `idxErr`, but `idx` is still passed to `installPlannedDeps`. `PluginIndex.Find` returns nil on a nil receiver, so `plugin_deps.go:152` reports that the dependency is not in the plugin index when the catalog simply never loaded, and that propagates as a non-zero exit even though the install succeeded and printed its success line — contradicting the contract stated at `plugin_group.go:289-290`. Suggested fix: when `idxErr != nil`, warn naming the index failure, point at `entire plugin doctor`, and skip dependency planning instead of calling it with a nil index.
==========================================================================================
id: 019fd8cf-9a24-7e27-80b9-c50148e16d41 | sev: medium
`cmd/entire/cli/plugin_deps.go:336, :402, :410` — the doctor reinstall fix cannot succeed on the plugins it flags. `checkManagedBinaryIntegrity` reports `Unverified` installs at `:383`, then suggests `entire plugin install <url> --force` at `:336`, `:402`, and `:410` — which re-runs `downloadPluginAsset` with `allowUnverified=false` and fails with `errUnverifiedAsset` for exactly those plugins. So `entire plugin doctor` exits 1 and hands the user a command that cannot work. Suggested fix: append ` --allow-unverified` to those three `Fix` strings when `m.Unverified`.
==========================================================================================
id: 019fd8ce-d599-704b-bd68-d26727dc8007 | sev: high
`cmd/entire/cli/plugin_install_remote.go:134-144` — on a bare `install <url>`, `--force` can replace a *different* installed plugin. `expectedName` is empty on that path (`plugin_group.go:237` sets it only in the index branch), so the name-reconciliation guard at `:134` is skipped and the remote-declared `name:` in `entire-plugin.yml` decides which `pkg/<name>/` and `bin/entire-<name>` get overwritten — under a confirmation that only named a URL. This is the same escalation the change closes on the index, dependency, and upgrade paths, and `plugin doctor` steers users into it: `plugin_deps.go:336`, `:402`, and `:410` all suggest `entire plugin install <repo-url> --force`.
